summary: Intermittent GPU availability on dedicated pool causing unpredictable throughput and elevated tail latency
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent drops in sustained throughput from their dedicated GPU pool beginning 2026-03-09 21:00 UTC. Symptoms include sudden increases in 95th/99th percentile latency, dropped streaming connections, and a spike in scheduler 'no available GPUs' errors for short windows (30-120s). Impact: Customer production features experiencing user-facing slowdowns and request throttling.

Impact:
- Throughput degraded by up to 40% during short windows.
- Tail latency increased from typical ~120ms to 800-2,500ms during events.
- Affected customer endpoints: batch inference + streaming chat.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: beta-dedicated-14 (us-east-1)
- Instance GPUs: mixed A100-80GB and A100-40GB nodes
- Autoscaler policy: aggressive downscale after 5m of low utilization

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Send sustained steady traffic at 70% of pool capacity for 30 minutes
2) Observe occasional short-lived drops in allocation and spikes in request queueing
3) Collect logs: scheduler shows transient allocation errors and kube events show pod eviction-like messages

Logs & links:
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/PU6p7/dedicated-pool-beta-dedicated-14
- Incident slack thread: #support-beta-14 (linked)
- K8s node events sample: "Device plugin: failed to allocate GPU: resource temporarily unavailable"
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC - Customer (BetaScale SRE): We see the pattern ~every 20-45 minutes. It lasts less than 2 minutes but causes our consumer-facing jobs to timeout. Attaching sample logs in Slack.
2026-03-10 09:30 UTC - Support (Asha Patel): Acknowledged. Collecting scheduler and node metrics; please preserve any pod-level logs for the next occurrence.

2026-03-10 11:05 UTC - SRE (Diego Ramirez): Found correlated node-level GPU allocation failures and a brief surge in system interrupts on two A100-40GB hosts. Opening infra ticket to correlate with host telemetry.
2026-03-11 02:20 UTC - Customer (BetaScale SRE): After we briefly reduced requested batch sizes, events reduced but did not disappear. We need a safe mitigator while you investigate.
2026-03-11 08:40 UTC - Support (Diego Ramirez): Implemented temporary per-tenant request rate cap and pinned routing to A100-80GB subset. Monitoring for 24h.
2026-03-12 13:15 UTC - Support (Asha Patel): Noted engineering follow-up for autoscaler hysteresis and device plugin update. Planned maintenance window requested.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 - Initial triage: Pattern consistent with short-lived GPU allocation failures rather than long node outages. Eviction count spikes aligned with scheduler 'allocation failed' metrics.
2026-03-10 - Telemetry: GPU utilization across pool remained variable; two A100-40GB hosts reported higher error counters in device plugin logs (retry errors, 'resource temporarily unavailable').
"2026-03-10 - Hypothesis:" Noisy tenant causing kernel-level GPU contention (driver/GPU-side preemption) leading to allocation retries and scheduler backpressure.

2026-03-11 - Autoscaler review: Downscale threshold too aggressive for mixed-capacity pools; when brief allocation failures occur autoscaler interprets as low utilization and removes nodes, amplifying short windows into user-visible capacity gaps.
2026-03-11 - Reproduction attempt: Simulated noisy workload with small memory-heavy kernels on A100-40GB nodes reproduced brief allocation failures and increased pod pending counts.
2026-03-12 - Cross-team notes: Kernel driver update candidate in staging; device-plugin bump proposed in PR github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4521 with retry/backoff improvements.
2026-03-12 - Risk assessment: Immediate customer impact moderate; potential recurrence until autoscaler hysteresis and mixed-node scheduling policy adjusted.

2026-03-12 - Next steps agreed: 1) maintain temporary routing pin to A100-80GB, 2) apply device-plugin backoff patch in canary, 3) tune autoscaler to use longer downscale window for this pool, 4) schedule capacity increase if behavior persists.
2026-03-12 - Notes on mitigation: Request rate cap introduced; observed reduced 95th/99th spikes by ~60% during test window.
resolution_notes: Mitigations applied 2026-03-11: pinned BetaScale routing to A100-80GB subset and introduced a conservative per-tenant request cap. Device-plugin backoff patch was deployed to a canary host (PR github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4521). Autoscaler config changed to 10m downscale window for beta-dedicated-14 to avoid amplifying transient allocation errors. Short-term outcome: tail latency spikes reduced and allocation failures frequency down ~70% in 24h observation. Follow-ups: schedule full roll-out of device-plugin fix, review mixed-node scheduling policy for heterogeneous pools, and offer customer option to increase reserved capacity if they need lower variance SLA. Customer notified and monitoring remains In Progress until 2026-03-16 verification window completes.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-ops: Roll device-plugin patch to all dedicated pools after successful canary (owner: Samir Kothari)
ENG-plat: Add autoscaler hysteresis flag for mixed-capacity pools and default to 10m for dedicated tiers (owner: Maya Chen)
CS: Offer BetaScale a temporary reserved capacity uplift for next billing period while we stabilize (owner: Priya Nair)
